response.text:
### 1) What is on the screen
The frame shows only the left ~112 pixels of a playfield against a huge black void. Top left is night sky with single-pixel stars over a flat medium-blue block, middle left is a flat green grandstand block with a tiny white-bordered scoreboard reading BAS / SOL, bottom left is a fence / dugout stripe, and a small white ball with a dithered trail sits alone at center-bottom. The eye goes first to the white ball-trail at x,y,width,height 152,200,48,12 because it is the only high-contrast thing in 66.2% black. The player is being asked to do nothing - no PRESS START, no score, no cue.

### 2) Does it look like a real NES game
(a) PASS - palette count reads as NES: measured 8 distinct colours, all 64-entry NES palette, well under the 25 on-screen ceiling of 12 background + 12 sprite + 1 backdrop.
(b) PASS - shading is flat, one colour per shape, no gradient banding in the blue at 0,32,112,48 or green at 0,112,96,64.
(c) FAIL - sprites do not read: the ball at 152,200,16,8 is 2-3 white pixels wide and its trail dissolves into 1-pixel dither that shares white with text, no clear 8x8 / 8x16 silhouette.
(d) PASS - no anti-aliasing and no soft edges anywhere; sky, stand, text, and trail are all hard 1-pixel steps as required at 256 x 240.
(e) FAIL - background colour changes do not stay on the 16 x 16 attribute grid: the white BAS/SOL box at 32,144,32,24 punches white/black inside a solid green 16x16 cell, and single-pixel star noise at 0,0,112,32 changes colour inside cells instead of by whole 16x16 zones.

Measured numbers do not contradict this: 8 colours and all-NES entries is why (a) and (b) pass, the failure is layout/attributes, not count.

### 3) Composition and text
Crowded into a left strip x 0-112, empty everywhere else: region 112,0,144,240 is solid black, ~56% of the frame. Focal point is the ball-trail in the void, not where the player needs it, which should be the stand / action on the left. Only legible text region is 32,144,32,24, two rows: Row1 BAS, Row2 SOL, white on green with white border. Worst is Row2 SOL at ~32,160,32,12: at 256x240 the glyphs are 5-6px tall, not on an 8x8 glyph grid, S/O close up and fill in, border touches letterforms, you have to guess if it is SOL / 50L / 5OL. No other text exists to explain the screen.

### 4) What looks AI generated or off
Not AI pillow-shading - this looks handmade and honest but broken, like a nametable that stops loading at x=112. Off in a human-bug way: 1) right 60% dead black void is a composition that reads as missing data, not design; 2) starfield is stray single pixels with no 8x8 tile structure; 3) ball trail is unstructured dither, detail without structure; 4) scoreboard border is not a whole number of 8x8 tiles, ~32x24 instead of 32x16 or 32x32; 5) blue sky rectangle ends in a hard vertical cut with no tile border or frame.

### 5) Five concrete fixes
1. Region [112,0,144,240] - fill the void by rule: extend the sky tile row from [0,32,112,48] right by 128 pixels in 16-pixel steps and extend field green, or set entire region to backdrop NES $0F Black with a proper 8-pixel tile border if intentional letterbox. Cannot ship half-nametable.
2. Region [32,144,32,24] - redraw text on glyph grid: delete box, redraw 4x 8x8 tiles, Row1 BAS + blank, Row2 BALL, NES $30 White on $0F Black, 8px cell per char, 1px internal padding from border moved out to 32x16 at 32,144,32,16.
3. Region [152,200,48,12] - rebuild projectile as real sprites: replace dither with one 8x8 ball sprite NES $30 White and one 8x8 motion ghost 50% checker, no 1-pixel fade, move whole shape left 8 pixels to 144,200 to clear scanline edge.
4. Region [0,0,112,32] - fix stars to tile law: erase all single blue/white stray pixels to NES $0F Black, then re-add 6 stars only at 8x8 tile centers using single NES $30 White pixel pairs, 8 pixels apart minimum.
5. Region [0,112,96,112] - snap attribute seams: move green stand right edge from ~96 to x=96 exactly and bottom fence at [0,192,56,32] to y=192 exactly, so all green/blue/black transitions land on 16x16 boundaries, replace fringe mixed-colour pixels with NES $2A Green and NES $12 Dark Blue.

### 6) Scores and machine readable block
nes_authenticity: 6/10 - colours and hard pixels are right, attributes and OAM discipline are not.
readability: 3/10 - one tiny illegible sign, no objective, ball lost in black.
charm: 3/10 - flat colours have honesty but no staging, humour, or finish.
